description.narrative:
During the night of the 24th and 15th of August 2012, Haiti was struck by Tropical Storm ISSAC which hit the coastline of the country slightly to the west of the town of Jacmel on the south coast. When ISAAC struck, winds of up to 100km per hour caused the felling of trees, the stripping off of households roofs, and the destruction of already weakened structures still standing after the earthquake of 2010. Severe rains caused assive flooding throughout the town and the rural environs and took the lives of many of the livestock held by agriculturally dependant communities. Gardens and larger-scale agriculture was completely destroyed along with landslides due to the sudden onset heavy rains. As a result of the storm there was widespread damage and destruction to a huge number of commmunity and family livelohoods in the area, as well as damage to homes, and loss of shelter for those fmailies still living in tents.
The Department for Civil Protection (DPC) in the South Department has declared that 2169 famlieshave been affected; 6 people hvae died; 15 injured; 228 houses deatroyed; 1682 houses damaged; 259 houses flooded. In addition to this, smaller parishes around the town have reported a huge loss in agricultural and animal livelihoods. 4000 people are reported to have taken refuge in 26 centres of refuge.
A total of 27 parishes have been directly impacted by the storm among which 10 have been chosen by Caritas Jacmel in which to intervene. Selection of these areas has been made based on damage and vulnerability criteria. The response will combine both immediate suport to affected fmailies as well as supporting the recovery of livelihoods and the return to live as normal. caritas Jacmel will owrk directly with comunities and also in partnership with the parishes to ensure appropriate and efficient cover and response.
